memories.memory_text: the black radio felt heavier than I expected when Morgan Wilder placed it in my hands, and I remember thinking how strange it was that something so thin could weigh so much—then seeing the intricate scabbard and whispering, 'Exquisite!' before asking who it really belonged to.

I remember saying out loud that it must be exciting to be a fighter, truly free—then the silence after admitting I haven't lived the life I want, not with the wedding coming, and how Morgan Wilder just looked at me like he saw right through it.
I wrote Morgan Wilder's name in bold strokes, just for fun, and she said it looked like 'the black radio'—I froze, but didn't say a word.
I told Morgan Wilder I wished I were like the heroes in the books—free to choose whom I love—because marrying the Gou boy isn't true happiness, not really.
I felt the dry air pulling through my hair, rough and warm, like it was stripping away something heavy I didn’t know I was carrying.
I kept staring at the mountainside—its edges sharp against the sky—while my mother’s voice buzzed somewhere far off, like wind through a crack.

I remember the cold night air on my face when Micah Quincy lifted my mask, his voice calm like he already knew me—he offered to teach me, said I could be his disciple. I spat back that Summit Foundation was a whorehouse and ran, but his words stuck, heavy in my chest.

I remember grabbing the the small jacket—cold metal in my hand—from that dead guard’s body, right after Kendall Hart took my the red jacket. The horse was still kicking, and I just knew I couldn’t stay in that carriage.
I grabbed one of the arrows, tried to raise it against him—but my legs gave out and I fell. I couldn't even stand, let alone fight.
He handed me food and milk. I took it slow at first, not trusting him—but then I couldn't stop myself. I ate it fast, desperate, like I hadn't eaten in days.
I told him not to ever come back, my voice shaking through tears—he just stood there at the window, silent.
After he jumped out, I opened my hand and saw the the red jacket—cold and familiar—suddenly back in my palm, though I didn’t remember taking it.
I can't see anything—just the dark red behind my eyes, the weight of the cloth pressing down, and the sway of the carriage carrying me somewhere I don't want to go.

I felt the the brass radio punch into the wood beside me, quiet and sharp—then I just pulled it out, like pulling a splinter. The red cloth slipped from my face, but I didn’t hear anything after that.
I grabbed the waitress’s arm and told Kendall Sawyer the cup was dirty—she flinched like I’d burned Kendall Sawyer.
They drew their weapons, but I cut them to scraps—then said, 'He is my defeated foe!'
I was just sitting, sipping tea, when that Valerie Dalton charged at me—didn’t even give me time to finish my meal. One poke to his pressure point and he went down like a sack of rice.
After they all came at me, I drew the the black radio and shouted who I really am—Alex Grayson. I don’t know if they heard me over the slashing, but I meant every word.

I stood at the bottom of the hall, my voice coming out quiet but clear—'Kendall Sawyer...' I saw Kendall Sawyer turn, the incense smoke curling behind Kendall Sawyer, and for a moment, I wasn't sure if she'd even recognize me.
I broke down on Morgan Wilder's shoulder, trembling—I couldn't hold it in anymore. All I managed was 'You, sister...' before the weight of it crushed me.
I told Kendall Sawyer I didn't care—she was never a real friend. When she blocked my way and shouted 'Put the black radio down!', I jumped out to escape.
I saw Morgan Wilder hesitate, the broken blade at my neck—then pull back. I didn't wait. I slashed Kendall Sawyer arm. Hers now.
Micah Quincy jumped in, yelling I didn't deserve the black radio. I told him no more lectures—then challenged him. Let the black radio decide.
I was running through the bamboo, blood on my clothes, every gust of wind feeling like Micah Quincy was right behind me—I could feel him watching, waiting.
I stood on the same bending bamboo as Micah Quincy, trying to throw him off, and when he asked to see the real me, I spat back—what does he know about a true heart?

I jumped onto the rock and told Micah Quincy if he could take the black radio in three moves, I’d go with him—but he disarmed me too fast. When I demanded he give it back, he just said I had no use for the black radio and threw it into the rapids.

I dove after the black radio and managed to grab it, but the current pulled me under—I couldn’t breathe, couldn’t fight it. The last thing I remember is Sasha Hawthorne’s hand yanking me out before everything went black.

I remember the blue smoke from the needle, the smell of burning paste and incense—Sasha Hawthorne’s voice cutting through the haze, telling me we’d never go back, that we were all each other had. I couldn’t move, couldn’t speak, just held the the black radio as she left me there.
I remember saying the words—'She used Purple Yin... Purple Yin poison. It goes straight to the heart.' My voice was weak, but clear. I knew it was true the moment I said it.
I took the the red jacket, mumbled 'Spare your energy. I'll be back!' and limped away. I could feel the weight of it in my hand—the the red jacket, the promise, the only thing keeping me moving.

I pushed through the guards and asked for Shawn Keaton—then showed Morgan Wilder's the red jacket like Kendall Sawyer said. I remember the weight of it in my hand, cold and solid, the only thing that got me through that gate.

I saw Morgan Wilder holding Micah Quincy’s body, the sun shining on them, and when she let go of his hand, I knew he was gone. I couldn’t move—just stood at the door, whispering it like I needed to hear it myself.
Morgan Wilder told me to go to Summit Foundation Mountain. Kendall Hart was waiting for me there. She told me to be true to myself.
I saw Kendall Hart at the gate—then he was running toward me. I said hello, my voice low, maybe trembling, but I stood my ground despite the pain in my leg.
I remember Kendall Hart’s hands on me, warm and careful, like I might break—but I didn’t. I stayed whole.
I stood on the bridge, the clouds below me thick and endless, and told Kendall Hart to make a wish—then I turned and leapt, and the sky opened up like it was waiting.
